screening_results.reason: Excluded because abstract reports fMRI social-cognition in patients with schizophrenia but does not report any healthy adult control group. Inclusion met: I1 (fMRI during a social-related task). Inclusion not met: I2 (at least one healthy participants group age 18–65) not demonstrated. Exclusion criteria met: none (E1 not applicable).

Abstract reports fMRI in normal adult volunteers viewing videos of positive and negative social encounters (dynamic social stimuli), satisfying I1. Participant age range (18–65) is not specified, so I2 cannot be confirmed from the abstract. No exclusion criteria met. Include for full-text review to verify participant ages and additional details.

The study used functional MRI to measure brain activity during kinship-related social scenarios evoking affiliative emotion, meeting I1 (social-related fMRI task). The abstract describes human participants with no indication of clinical populations, implying healthy adults, satisfying I2. No exclusion criteria apply.

Study used task-based BOLD fMRI while participants made social-related (affiliation vs isolation) judgments, clearly satisfying I1. The abstract indicates healthy younger and older adult groups but does not report ages, so I2 cannot be fully confirmed from the abstract alone; include for full-text review to verify age ranges.

fMRI study presenting love and power-related movie clips (social motivations) to healthy adult participants (n=17); directly examines neural correlates of affiliation and power, meeting task-based social processing and healthy adult criteria.

fMRI study explicitly examines social interaction context vs solitary context during encoding and retrieval—addresses social-related processing (I1). Abstract does not specify participant ages or explicit healthy status, so I2 cannot be confirmed from the abstract; include for full-text review to verify participant characteristics.

This is an fMRI study of participants observing social interactions with gaze manipulation, addressing social cognition—meets I1. The abstract does not specify participant ages or health status, so I2 cannot be confirmed; include for full-text review.

Participants are children aged 8–12, so the study does not include healthy adult participants aged 18–65 and fails inclusion criterion I2. Although it uses fMRI for social tasks (I1), it does not meet the age requirement for this review.

Abstract reports an fMRI study where participants experienced social interaction (gaze and socially relevant facial expressions) versus observation, matching social-related processing. While participant ages and explicit statement of health are not given, this is a primary fMRI study of social cognition in humans; include for full-text to confirm demographics/health status.

fMRI was used while participants observed others' regret (a social cognitive task involving Perception and Understanding of Others), satisfying I1. The abstract does not report participant ages or explicitly state they were healthy adults (I2 not demonstrated), so include for full-text review to confirm eligibility.

fMRI study where participants categorized prosodic expressions to infer speakers' communicative intentions (social communication), meeting the social-related task requirement. Abstract does not report participant ages, so inclusion regarding age cannot be fully confirmed from abstract; include for full-text review.

Abstract reports an fMRI study in healthy adult participants using real-time fMRI neurofeedback to modulate affiliative emotion (tenderness/affection) versus control emotion (pride). This addresses social-related processing (Affiliation/Attachment). Participants appear to be healthy adults. No exclusion criteria met.

Abstract reports event-related fMRI responses to social (face) and non-social targets, meeting I1. Participant characteristics (health status and age range) are not specified, so I2 cannot be confirmed; per rules, include for full-text review.

fMRI was used while participants engaged in live, contingent social interactions and joint attention tasks (social cognitive processing). The abstract implies a typical healthy participant sample with no clinical groups reported. Thus inclusion criteria I1 and I2 are met.

fMRI study where participants performed social-cognitive tasks (face processing, emotion recognition, affective ToM) and included a group of healthy matched controls. Abstract lacks explicit participant ages (18–65), so inclusion criterion I2 cannot be fully confirmed from abstract alone; include for full-text review.

Study uses fMRI of working memory in persons with multiple sclerosis and does not examine social-related processing (I1 not met). Abstract does not indicate presence of a healthy adult group (I2 not met). This is not a review (E1 not met). Therefore excluded.

Abstract indicates an fMRI study of deception (suggesting a social-related task) but provides insufficient information about participant characteristics (whether healthy adults aged 18–65 were included). No exclusion criteria are met. Include for full-text review to confirm I2.

This is an fMRI study probing empathy and social cognition through viewing social/emotional scenes, satisfying I1. The abstract describes human participants and interindividual differences suggesting healthy volunteers; age range not stated but likely adult healthy sample, so include for full-text to confirm I2.

Abstract reports an fMRI study of social interaction (self- and other-initiated joint attention) in 24 healthy adult participants (ages within 18–65), meeting the review scope. No exclusion criteria are met. Recommend inclusion for full-text review.

Sample consists of adolescents rather than adults (not within 18–65), and the fMRI task (Monetary Incentive Delay) is a monetary reward task rather than an explicitly social-related task. Therefore the study does not meet inclusion criteria I1 or I2 based on the abstract.

Functional MRI was used while healthy adult participants read scenarios evoking moral emotions (disgust, indignation), which probes social-related processing (moral judgment/attribution). The study reports 13 normal adult volunteers, satisfying the healthy adult sample requirement. No exclusion criteria are met from the abstract.

Abstract suggests fMRI-assessed neural responses to social interaction images in remitted depression, but does not explicitly state that a functional MRI task was used or that healthy adult participants (ages 18–65) were included as a group. Insufficient methodological and sample details in the abstract to confirm inclusion criteria, so include for full-text review.

Abstract reports an fMRI study of implicit facial emotion processing (a social-related task), satisfying I1. The abstract does not report inclusion of a healthy adult (18–65) control group or participant ages, so I2 is not demonstrated from the abstract. No exclusion criteria met. Recommend full-text review to confirm presence of healthy adult participants.

Study used fMRI during a facial emotional processing task (a social-related task) and included a matched healthy control group of adults. Although exact ages are not reported in the abstract, participants are described as adults; no exclusion criteria (e.g., review article) apply. Include for full-text review to confirm age range falls within 18–65 and extract relevant data.

fMRI study of sarcasm detection used scenario-reading social task engaging mentalizing/social cognition in 20 normal adult volunteers. This meets I1 (social-related task during fMRI) and I2 (healthy adult participants). Not a review/meta-analysis, so no exclusion criteria met. Include for full-text review.

Abstract reports an fMRI study in normal (healthy) subjects performing a social-related task (watching movie clips of social interactions), matching the review objective. No exclusion criteria apply. Age range not specified but 'normal subjects' implies healthy adults; include for full-text confirmation.
Participants are children (mean age 10.2 years), not adults. The review requires at least one group of healthy participants aged 18–65 (I2), so this study does not meet inclusion criteria.

The fMRI experiment examined processing of social communication (facial expressions and social hand gestures) during observation and execution, meeting I1. The abstract implies human participants and does not mention clinical populations; age range not reported, so per guidelines include for full-text review to confirm healthy adults 18–65 (I2). No exclusion criteria met.

fMRI task explicitly investigates social cognition (mental state inference from film extracts) satisfying I1. The study includes healthy control groups, but ages 18–65 are not specified in the abstract, so I2 is uncertain. No exclusion criteria met. Include for full-text review to confirm participant ages and other details.

Excluded because I1 is not met: the study used resting-state fMRI (no social-related task was performed). I2 is not demonstrated in the abstract (ages 18–65 not reported), so cannot be confirmed. No exclusion criteria (E1) apply. Inclusion criteria met: none. Inclusion criteria not met or not demonstrated: I1 not met; I2 not demonstrated.

Abstract reports event-related fMRI responses to positive social stimuli, satisfying I1. It appears to study depressed participants pre/post-treatment but does not report inclusion of a healthy adult control group (I2 not demonstrated). Not a review/meta-analysis (E1 not met). Insufficient information about healthy participants—include for full-text review.

Includes fMRI of dynamic facial-expression processing with social interaction cues (meets I1). The non-SPD comparison group appears to be healthy, but participant ages (18–65) are not specified in the abstract, so I2 cannot be confirmed from abstract alone. Not a review (E1 not met). Include for full-text review to verify participant ages and health status.

Abstract describes dual-fMRI hyperscanning while pairs performed an interactive social-exchange task, meeting I1. The abstract does not specify participant ages or that they were healthy adults, so I2 cannot be confirmed from the abstract; include for full-text review to verify I2.

Abstract reports an event-related fMRI paradigm using dynamic social vs nonsocial gestures, addressing social processing (meets I1). The abstract does not specify participant health status or ages (I2 unclear). Because participant details are insufficient, include for full-text review to confirm healthy adult sample.

Exclusion criteria met: none. Inclusion criteria met: I1 (fMRI during social-related tasks—responses to emotional words and facial emoticons). Inclusion criteria not met: I2 (no healthy adult participants aged 18–65; sample comprised adolescents with ASD only).

The study used event-related fMRI (with simultaneous EEG) while healthy adult participants viewed and processed others' emotional facial expressions—clearly a social-related perception task (empathy/understanding of others). Participants were healthy adults (mean age 29±6). Not a review or meta-analysis. Abstract provides sufficient information to meet inclusion criteria.

fMRI study of healthy adult participants (n=16) viewing and interpreting verbal and non-verbal social interactions, i.e., a social-related task. Meets inclusion criteria I1 and I2; not a systematic review/meta-analysis. Abstract provides sufficient information to include for full-text review.

Abstract reports a combined fMRI and eye-tracking study contrasting social interaction vs. observation, meeting I1 (fMRI during social task). The abstract does not specify participant ages or explicitly state participants were healthy (I2 not demonstrated). No exclusion criteria met. Include for full-text review to confirm participant characteristics and eligibility.

Abstract reports functional MRI during live reciprocal imitation of hand gestures, a social cognitive task. Participant health/age not specified in abstract, so I2 cannot be confirmed from abstract alone; include for full-text review.

Includes fMRI during a social-related task (EmpaToM) addressing social affect and cognition, meeting I1. The abstract does not specify participant health status or ages 18–65, so I2 is not confirmed from the abstract. No exclusion criteria are met. Include for full-text review to confirm participant characteristics and eligibility.

EXCLUDED because inclusion criterion I1 not met: study used resting-state fMRI rather than a task-based social fMRI paradigm. Inclusion criterion I2 is met (healthy control group present). No exclusion criteria (E1) apply.

Abstract describes an fMRI hyperscanning study of dyadic shared attention (mutual and joint gaze), a social-processing task. Health status and exact ages of participants are not specified in the abstract, so full-text review is needed to confirm I2.

fMRI study of a social interaction task (handshake with virtual avatar) including a healthy control group; however ages of participants (18–65) are not reported in the abstract, so full text is needed to confirm I2.

No healthy adult group was recruited. Exclusion IDs met: none. Inclusion IDs met: I1 (fMRI during social-related tasks: Facial Affect Matching and Mental State Attribution; rs-fMRI). Inclusion IDs not met: I2 (no group of healthy participants aged 18–65).

Abstract reports an fMRI study using a social interaction (virtual ball-toss) task that probes social reward processing, meeting I1. Participant sample (n=38) is given but health status and ages (18–65) are not specified; therefore include for full-text review to confirm I2.

Study used fMRI during a social-interaction task (ultimatum game) to predict decisions in volunteers, meeting social-processing task requirement. Participants are described as volunteers (healthy adults), satisfying inclusion of healthy adult group. No exclusion criteria apply.

fMRI study examining perception of social interactions (dyadic interactions vs non-interactive actions), meeting I1. The abstract does not state participant ages or explicit healthy status, so I2 cannot be confirmed from abstract; include for full-text review.

Abstract reports an fMRI study of self–other social processing (adjective judgments about self vs other) and includes a matched typically developing healthy control group of young adults. Fits I1 (social-related fMRI task) and I2 (healthy participants aged 18–65). No exclusion criteria met.

fMRI study where participants performed a social-related task (discriminating social interactions from neutral movements), and the sample includes healthy adults aged 20–41 (within 18–65). Thus it meets I1 and I2; no exclusion criteria apply.

No evidence the study used task-based fMRI (I1 not demonstrated) and abstract focuses on patients with degenerative cerebellar atrophy with no mention of a healthy adult group (I2 not demonstrated). Not a review/meta-analysis (E1 not met).

The study reports fMRI data collected while healthy adults performed mental-state judgments about naturalistic social interactions (a social cognition task), satisfying I1 and I2. It is an original empirical study, not a review.

Abstract reports an fMRI study in healthy adults (n=24) where participants modulated voice to express social traits (affiliation, competence), meeting I1 and I2. No exclusion criteria (e.g., review/meta-analysis) are met. Include for full-text review.

fMRI data were acquired while participants viewed photographs of actors (social perception/face learning) before and after brief social interactions, satisfying I1. The abstract describes healthy participants (no clinical groups reported), consistent with I2. No exclusion criteria are met.

fMRI was used to investigate neural correlates of learning Japanese Sign Language with social interaction vs DVD, addressing social communication processing; participants were healthy adults. While the abstract doesn't detail the exact in-scanner task, it clearly examines social-related language learning and reports fMRI outcomes, meeting inclusion criteria.

Study used fMRI during a social interaction task (iterated Prisoner’s Dilemma) in healthy subjects randomized to intranasal oxytocin or placebo — meets the review objective. Ages not specified in the abstract, so include for full-text review to confirm age range (18–65).

Abstract reports an fMRI study in 36 healthy adult participants investigating neural processing of social interactions (cooperativity and affectivity), meeting the review objective and inclusion criteria. Not a review/meta-analysis.

fMRI study of emotional prosody (social communication), which is a social-related task in humans. The abstract reports healthy subjects but does not specify ages 18–65, so inclusion of I2 is not confirmed; full-text review needed to verify participant ages and health details.

Abstract reports a neuroimaging study isolating brain responses to observed social interactions (point-light displays), indicating an fMRI/functional neuroimaging social-related task (satisfies I1). The abstract does not specify participant health status or ages (I2 unclear). Because age/health information is insufficient in the abstract, include for full-text review to confirm I2.

fMRI study of action prediction (perception/understanding of others) during a social task in expert athletes and novices; meets I1. Participant groups appear to be healthy adults but ages 18–65 are not specified in the abstract, so I2 is uncertain—include for full-text review.

This fMRI study uses naturalistic movie viewing to probe processing of social interactions (perception/understanding of others), satisfying I1. The abstract does not report participant ages or explicitly confirm they are healthy adults, so include for full-text review to verify I2.

fMRI study used a false-belief task probing understanding of others' mental states, satisfying I1 (social-related task). The abstract does not explicitly state participants were healthy adults aged 18–65, so I2 is not demonstrated from the abstract. No exclusion criteria apply. Include for full-text review to confirm participant health and ages.

The study used resting-state fMRI with no social-related task, so inclusion criterion I1 (task-based social processing fMRI) is not met. Healthy controls are reported but ages 18–65 are not specified, so I2 is not demonstrated. It is not a review/meta-analysis (E1 not met).

fMRI study of processing social interactions in healthy participants; meets I1. Ages 18–65 not specified in abstract so I2 is uncertain; no exclusion criteria met. Include for full-text review to confirm participant ages and other details.

This study used fMRI while healthy participants performed social-related tasks (eye-gaze detection, self-propelling motion, implicit mental-inference role-playing), addressing social perception and mentalizing. Participants are described as healthy (adult) subjects. No exclusion criteria apply.

fMRI study examining perception/understanding of others (third-person social interaction), satisfying I1. Abstract does not report participant health status or ages, so I2 cannot be confirmed; include for full-text review.

The study used fMRI to assess empathy (a social-cognitive process) in human participants, satisfying I1. The abstract describes human participants without indication of clinical populations, consistent with healthy adult samples; because ages are not specified I2 is likely but uncertain, so include for full-text review to confirm ages. No exclusion criteria are met.

The study used functional MRI to measure neural responses during a social task (gaze shifts/joint attention), satisfying I1. The abstract does not specify participant ages or explicitly state they were healthy (I2 cannot be confirmed from the abstract), so include for full-text review to verify I2.

Abstract reports task-based fMRI during a social interactive task (and a control), and experiments include healthy adult subjects; fits review objective of social processing in healthy adults. Not a review/meta-analysis.

Study used resting-state fMRI in adolescents with Internet addiction (ages 15–20); no social-related task reported (I1 not met) and participants are not healthy adults aged 18–65 (I2 not met). This is not a systematic review (E1 not met).

Abstract reports an fMRI study where participants made social inferences about others' emotions based on nonverbal and contextual cues, satisfying I1. The abstract does not state participant health status or ages (I2 not demonstrated). No exclusion criteria met. Include for full-text review to confirm participant characteristics.

The abstract describes two fMRI experiments on understanding intentions in social interactions—a social cognition task relevant to the review. While participant ages are not specified, the study appears to involve healthy adults; include for full-text review to confirm demographics.

fMRI face-encoding task clearly assesses social-related processing (face/social cognition). A healthy control group is present, but ages 18–65 are not specified in the abstract, so inclusion on age criterion (I2) is uncertain; full-text needed to confirm. No exclusion criteria met.

fMRI was conducted during social judgments of faces (trustworthiness/age), satisfying I1. The study included 18 nonclinical controls (healthy participants), satisfying I2. No exclusion criteria apply. Abstract provides sufficient evidence of social task and healthy adult controls; include for full-text review to confirm age range if needed.

The study used fMRI while participants viewed faces of political candidates (a social perception/understanding of others task) and involved healthy adult participants (registered Democrats and Republicans). Thus it meets I1 and I2. No exclusion criteria (e.g., not a review) apply. Include for full-text review.

Abstract reports an fMRI study where healthy adult participants performed a gaze-following task (social attention/gaze processing) involving political in-group/out-group faces — a social-related task. Participants are healthy voters (adults). Not a review. Therefore meets I1 and I2.

fMRI study of social communication with healthy control group present (I1 met). Abstract does not report participant ages, so I2 (healthy adults 18–65) cannot be confirmed from the abstract alone. Not a review/meta-analysis. Include for full-text review to confirm age range and extract data.

Abstract reports an fMRI study administering attachment-related (social) scenes to healthy adult participants (N=25). This satisfies I1 (social-related fMRI task) and I2 (healthy adults 18–65); no exclusion criteria met.

fMRI study of social cognition (theory of mind and empathy) in healthy human volunteers; meets I1. Participants described as healthy volunteers, but age range (18–65) not reported in abstract, so include for full-text confirmation of I2.

(a) Exclusion IDs met: none. (b) Inclusion IDs met: none clearly demonstrated. (c) Inclusion IDs not met/not demonstrated: I1 not met — Embedded Figures Task is a perceptual task, not a social-related task; I2 not demonstrated — abstract mentions control subjects but does not report ages or explicitly confirm healthy adults aged 18–65. Exclude based on abstract evidence.

I1 satisfied: fMRI performed during empathy and theory-of-mind comic-strip task (social cognition). I2 likely satisfied: sample are healthy college students (ages 17–21, mean 19.3) indicating adult participants in the eligible range, though abstract reports some 17-year-olds so exact age eligibility is uncertain; include for full-text review to confirm.

No healthy adult (18–65) participants: sample consists of adolescents with NSSI (and likely adolescent controls), so I2 not met. The study does appear to use fMRI during a simulated social interaction task (I1 met). No exclusion criteria (e.g., review) apply.

Excluded because participants are adolescents (mean age 16.98), so inclusion criterion I2 (at least one group aged 18–65) is not met. Inclusion I1 (fMRI during a social-related task) is met. No exclusion criteria (E1) apply.

fMRI was conducted while participants watched movies depicting emotions, and the study examines synchronization of brain activity related to understanding others' emotions and actions (meets social perception/understanding; I1). The abstract does not report participant ages or explicitly confirm they were healthy adults, so I2 cannot be confirmed from the abstract; include for full-text review to verify health status and ages.

fMRI was used while participants viewed and encoded social interactions (egocentric vs allocentric), meeting I1. The abstract does not specify participant health status or ages (I2 not demonstrated), and no exclusion criteria are met. Include for full-text review to confirm participant demographics and health.

fMRI task explicitly involves social cognition (virtual social cognition task) satisfying I1. Healthy control group (14) is present but ages 18–65 are not specified in the abstract, so I2 cannot be confirmed from abstract alone. No exclusion criteria met. Include for full-text review to confirm participant ages and extract data.

Study reports task-based fMRI during a validated social cognition (Theory of Mind) task in healthy human volunteers. Age range 18–65 not specified in abstract, so inclusion criterion I2 cannot be confirmed from abstract alone. No exclusion criteria met. Include for full-text review to confirm participant ages and further details.

Abstract reports examination of neural substrates of social cognition and face processing in a group of healthy young adults, meeting criterion I2. However, the abstract does not explicitly state that functional MRI was used or that participants performed an fMRI social task (I1). Insufficient information to confirm fMRI task-based methods, so include for full-text review.

Abstract reports an fMRI experiment investigating perception of socially relevant facial expressions (social communication), satisfying I1. Participant health status and ages are not specified in the abstract, so include for full-text review to confirm I2.

Abstract reports an fMRI study using a social working memory task probing social cognition and relates brain activity to trait perspective-taking, meeting social-task fMRI criterion. Participant health/ages not specified in abstract, but study likely uses healthy adults; given uncertainty, include for full-text review to confirm demographics.

fMRI study where participants performed praying, which the authors interpret as recruiting social-cognition networks (meets social-related task criterion). Participant group described as Danish Christians (likely healthy adults) but ages 18–65 not specified in abstract; include for full-text review to confirm age and health status.

fMRI was conducted while healthy volunteers performed a social interaction/game with various agents, addressing social processing (perception/understanding of others). The abstract does not report participant ages; full text needed to confirm age 18–65, so include for full-text review.

fMRI was used while participants viewed socio-cognitive (social-awareness campaign) videos; study compares drivers with frequent offenses and safe drivers (presumably healthy adult participants). The task probes social cognition (STS reactivity). Satisfies inclusion criteria I1 and I2.

fMRI study uses a social interactive task (Domino game) and includes healthy control participants, but abstract does not clearly state that healthy participants are within age 18–65. Include for full-text review to confirm age eligibility and extract relevant data.

Meets I1: fMRI was conducted while participants played an iterated Prisoner’s Dilemma (a social interaction task). I2 (healthy adults 18–65) is not explicitly confirmed in the abstract (participants described as 'male participants' but health status/age range not reported). No exclusion criteria met. Recommend full-text review to confirm participant health and age.

Abstract reports an fMRI study of social cognition (comparisons of close vs non-close others), meeting the social-related task criterion. Participant health and exact ages (18–65) are not specified in the abstract, so inclusion criterion I2 cannot be confirmed from abstract alone; include for full-text review.

Abstract reports an fMRI study measuring brain responses while participants viewed social interactions involving threat perception (meets I1). The abstract does not specify participant ages or health status (I2 not demonstrated), and no exclusion criteria are met. Include for full-text review to confirm participant demographics and health.

Exclusion criteria met: none (E1 not met). Inclusion criteria met: I1 (fMRI during a social-related facial emotion recognition task). Inclusion criteria not met: I2 not satisfied — sample includes only schizophrenia participants; no healthy adult (18–65) group reported.

The abstract describes an fMRI study of social working memory/social cognition, satisfying I1. Participant health status and ages are not reported in the abstract, so I2 cannot be confirmed; include for full-text review to verify presence of healthy adults 18–65.

Event-related fMRI was collected while participants performed a mind-perception task and related social attention was examined, satisfying I1 (social-related fMRI). The abstract does not specify participant ages or explicitly state they were healthy adults, so I2 cannot be confirmed from the abstract; include for full-text review to verify I2.

Abstract reports fMRI during a social task (prisoners' dilemma) and includes a healthy control group; age range (18–65) is not specified in the abstract, so I2 cannot be confirmed. No exclusion criteria (e.g., review) are met. Include for full-text review to confirm participant ages and extract details.

fMRI study using a valence classification task on agency and communion (social cognition)—meets I1. Abstract does not report participant health status or ages (18–65) so inclusion for full-text review is needed to confirm I2.

No task-based fMRI was reported: authors used resting-state fMRI and behavioral social-cognition tests (MASC, RMET), so I1 is not met. The abstract does report a control group but does not provide ages (18–65) required by I2, so I2 is not demonstrated. No exclusion criteria apply.

Abstract reports an fMRI study where healthy adult men performed social-cognitive tasks (face gaze processing and theory-of-mind tests). This meets I1 (social-related task during fMRI) and I2 (healthy participants aged within adult range). No exclusion criteria apply.

Meets I1: fMRI was conducted during a social-cognitive task (affective ToM, emotion recognition, neutral faces). A matched healthy control group is included, but participant ages (18–65) are not reported in the abstract so I2 cannot be confirmed. No exclusion criteria met. Include for full-text review to confirm ages and full methods.

Abstract addresses social cognition and neural activity in patients and unaffected siblings but does not explicitly state that fMRI was conducted or confirm a healthy adult control group aged 18–65. Because the abstract is insufficient to determine whether I1 and I2 are met but the study is likely relevant, include for full-text review.

fMRI study using a dynamic Ultimatum Game with on-line social interactions — meets I1 (social-related task during fMRI). Abstract does not specify participant health status or ages 18–65 (I2 not demonstrated). Not a review. Include for full-text review to confirm participant eligibility.

Functional MRI was used during a social interaction simulation probing friendship (social-affiliation/other-related processing) in 28 participants. The study clearly addresses social processing and reports neural activity during task. Participants are described as typical healthy subjects (no clinical groups mentioned), consistent with inclusion. No exclusion criteria apply.

Abstract reports an fMRI study of face emotion processing (a social-related task) in a community sample (likely healthy). Age range not specified, and health status/ages cannot be fully confirmed from the abstract, so include for full-text review to verify I2.

Abstract reports fMRI in healthy adult participants (15 healthy males) but does not clearly state that the scanned task was social (stimuli described only as "fear-inducing visual stimuli"). Because I1 (social-related task) is uncertain from the abstract, include for full-text review to confirm. I2 (healthy adults) is satisfied.

Abstract reports an fMRI study where participants judged faces as trustworthy/untrustworthy (social-related task) and includes a healthy control group; no exclusion criteria (not a review) are met. Include for full-text review.

No exclusion criteria met. Inclusion met: I1 (fMRI task assessing social cognition/ToM). Inclusion NOT met: I2 — sample are children aged 9–13, not healthy adults age 18–65 required for the review. Abstract clearly reports participant ages, so exclude based on age criterion.

fMRI was conducted while participants read a literary text that produced suspense and activated brain areas associated with social cognition, suggesting social-related processing; participant health/ages not specified in abstract, so full-text needed to confirm I2.

Exclusion IDs met: none (E1 not met). Inclusion IDs met: none. Inclusion IDs not met or not demonstrated: I1 — study used resting-state fMRI, not a social-related task; I2 — participants are childhood-onset and matched typically developing controls (pediatric), not healthy adults aged 18–65. Therefore excluded.

fMRI was performed while mothers viewed images of their own and unfamiliar child/dog, which is a social/attachment task (meets I1). Participants are adult mothers (healthy adult sample implied), meeting I2. No exclusion criteria met. Abstract provides sufficient information to include for full-text review.

Abstract reports an fMRI study of social decision-making (peer presence, theory-of-mind related regions)—meets I1. Includes healthy young adult participants (ages 21–22) within 18–65—meets I2. No exclusion criteria met (not a review/meta-analysis).

Abstract reports fMRI during a social-related task (scanner-adapted Multifaceted Empathy Test) and includes an age- and gender-matched control group. Age range 18–65 for the healthy controls is not explicitly stated in the abstract, so inclusion on I2 is uncertain; full-text needed to confirm age eligibility.

Abstract reports an fMRI study of subjects observing an expert demonstrator, explicitly investigating social-cognitive processes (recognition of intentions, motor resonance, mentalizing), meeting I1. Participant health and ages are not specified in the abstract, so I2 cannot be confirmed from abstract alone. No exclusion criteria apply. Include for full-text review to confirm participant ages/health and other details.

Abstract reports an fMRI study where mothers’ brain responses to emotional expressions of their own children were compared—this is a social-related task (perception/attachment). Participants are adult mothers (healthy adult group). No exclusion criteria apply. Full text recommended to confirm participant ages and health status.

Excluded because the study includes only schizophrenia participants and no healthy adult group was reported (I2 not met). The study does use fMRI during an emotion-recognition task (I1 met). No exclusion criteria (E1) apply.

Abstract reports fMRI BOLD imaging during simulated face-to-face social interactions (viewing actresses describing happy/unhappy experiences), with 21 healthy young adult participants indicating subjective emotion onset. This meets I1 (social-related task during fMRI) and I2 (healthy adults 18–65). Not a review; no exclusion criteria met. Recommend full-text review to confirm ages and task details.

Abstract reports fMRI during a visually based social judgment task (evaluating social dominance in faces) in a sample of 23 healthy adults, matching the review’s focus on social-related processing in healthy adults. No exclusion criteria apply.

fMRI was used while participants performed a social cognition task (inferring others' emotions and learning from feedback), which meets I1. The abstract does not specify participant age/health, so include for full-text review to confirm I2.

fMRI was used with theory-of-mind (social cognition) tasks, meeting I1. The study includes a healthy control group, but ages 18–65 are not specified in the abstract so I2 is not confirmed. No exclusion criteria are met. Recommend full-text review to verify participant ages and extract data.

Event-related fMRI in healthy human subjects performing social communication task (gaze and pointing) directly addresses social processing. Abstract confirms I1 but does not state participant ages (18–65), so include for full-text review to confirm I2.

Abstract indicates study of neural responses to social/emotional stimuli in schizophrenia and depression but does not explicitly state use of fMRI or inclusion of healthy adult controls (ages 18–65). Not a review. Insufficient information to determine inclusion, so include for full-text review to confirm imaging modality and participant groups.

Exclusion criteria met: none (E1 not met). Inclusion criteria met: I1 (fMRI during social-related tasks—face processing and affect labeling). Inclusion criteria not met: I2 (no healthy adult participants aged 18–65; sample are boys aged 10–18). Thus study is excluded.

This is an fMRI study where participants viewed and categorized threatening vs. teasing social interactions, satisfying I1 (social-related fMRI task). The abstract does not specify participant ages or explicitly state they were healthy adults 18–65 (I2 not demonstrated). No exclusion criteria met. Include for full-text review to confirm participant health/age and other details.

fMRI experimental task contrasts anticipation of touching an animate (human) vs inanimate target, qualifying as social-related processing (I1). Participants are described as healthy volunteers, but ages 18–65 are not reported in the abstract, so I2 is uncertain—include for full-text review to confirm age. Not a review/meta-analysis.
